lines: Stereo effects processor in four sections: a filter, a resonator, a ping-pong echo and an ambience reverb, with a modulation source and per-knob CV and randomisation mapping
Sets the cutoff of the filter, from 10Hz to 22000Hz
Picks the filter type: lowpass, bandpass, highpass or comb
Moves the filter to one of four points in the chain, before or after the resonator, the echo and the ambience

Sets how far the modulation source moves the parameters that have been mapped to it
Sets the rate of the modulation source
Picks the modulation shape: random, sine, ramp, inverted ramp, square, sample and hold, or envelope follower

Sets how much of the resonator's output is fed back into it
Sets the delay time of a two-tap stereo ping-pong echo, 10ms fully anti-clockwise out to 6 seconds fully clockwise; with a clock patched into SYNC the time is quantised to divisions of it

Sets how many times the echo repeats
Sets the size, tone and direction of the ambience: smallest and brightest in the middle, biggest and darkest at either end, and running the input backwards below the middle
Pans the ambience from side to side on its own
Sets how long the ambience takes to die away

Sets how much echo is mixed with the dry signal; when a cable is in the ECHO jack this attenuates that CV instead
Sets how much ambience is mixed with the dry signal; when a cable is in the AMBIENCE jack this attenuates that CV instead
Picks what MAP applies to the knobs: randomisation, CV mapping, or modulation
Held down, it turns the knobs and buttons over to their second function

Applies the mapping for whichever target the map mode names, so that turning a knob then sets that amount rather than the value
Wipes the mapping amounts for whichever target the map mode names
Sets how far the modulation source moves this parameter, from nothing to its full range
Sets how far the CV input moves this parameter, from nothing to its full range
Sets how far a randomisation event moves this parameter, from nothing to its full range
The left side of the signal going in, and with nothing patched on the right it feeds both sides in mono
The right side of the signal going in
Sets the dry and wet balance of that section, 0V to 5V, attenuated by that section's own mix knob
A clock for the time-based sections; with it patched the echo time snaps to divisions of the clock
A rising edge here fires a randomisation of everything the random mapping covers
Shifts the filter cutoff, -5V to 10V, scaled by the cutoff CV amount set through MAP
Shifts the resonator tuning, -5V to 10V, scaled by the tune CV amount set through MAP
Shifts the echo time, -5V to 10V, scaled by the echo CV amount set through MAP
Shifts the ambience spacetime, -5V to 10V, scaled by the spacetime CV amount set through MAP
The left side of the finished signal
The right side of the finished signal
Menu — Knob mode — fixes which layer the knobs edit without a button held down: Normal, Alt (hold Shift), Mod, CV or Rnd
Menu — Use native VCV randomisation — hands randomising over to Rack's own; off by default
Menu — Randomise slew time — a slider setting how long a randomisation takes to slew into place, from 0 to 10 seconds, and 0.2 seconds by default
Note — the resonator, echo and ambience mix knobs all come up fully dry, so the input passes through the filter alone until one of them is turned up.
Note — the Randomise slew time slider on the menu is greyed out while Use native VCV randomisation is switched on.
Iroi.notes: The DSP for this module is not in the public repository, so the filter position ordering and the exact ranges of the resonator and ambience controls come from the maker's tooltips and the panel, not from code. The randomise slew time (param 48) is a menu slider with no place on the panel, so it is untagged and covered by a Menu line. A SYNC label appears on the panel near the MOD LEVEL knob with no control of its own at that spot; what it marks could not be settled. The docs/ folder of the source carries a manual for Befaco Oneiroi, which is a different and larger module; nothing in it was used here. The left and right inputs take a polyphonic cable and sum every channel to one (Iroi.cpp:765); the module itself is mono, and the maker does not tag it Polyphonic.

Sets how many steps long that channel's loop is, from 1 to 32
A short press cycles that channel's looping between off, a locked loop, and a loop that mutates a step now and then; a long press opens that row's menu page, and a very long press resets the channel
A rising edge draws a new value on that channel, subject to its divider and its probability
That channel's random voltage, after gain, offset, quantising and slew

Menu — Save preset — writes the whole state into one of eight slots, each listed as used or unused
Menu — Performance Mode — leaves the menu pages and puts the eight knobs back to the channel gain setting
Menu — Preset — shows the preset page, where the eight channel buttons load and save the eight preset slots
Menu — Divider — puts the eight channel knobs on the divider setting
Menu — Probability — puts the eight channel knobs on the probability setting
Menu — Style — puts the eight channel knobs on the random style setting
Menu — Offset — puts the eight channel knobs on the offset setting
Menu — Scale — puts the eight channel knobs on the quantiser scale setting
Menu — Slide — puts the eight channel knobs on the slide setting

Note — hold a channel button for about a second and let go to open that button's page; a click on any button then returns to the performance panel.
Random8.notes: Each channel has one physical knob carrying eight stacked parameters, one per menu page, so those eight indices all sit at the same panel position and each has its own line. The channel buttons double as the menu page buttons, which is why one line covers both roles.
